question: Does grokking arise because a fast memorising circuit and a slower generalising circuit compete under weight decay, with the generalising circuit eventually winning because it produces larger useful logits per unit parameter norm, and does the resulting dataset-size crossover predict ungrokking and semi-grokking?

key_findings.claim: The paper's clearest contribution is a dataset-dependent circuit-efficiency hypothesis that turns an existing fast-memoriser/slow-generaliser story into two distinctive qualitative predictions: dataset-shrink ungrokking and long-lived partial-generalisation plateaus.
key_findings.evidence: The proposed mechanism combines three ingredients: two train-fitting algorithms with different test behavior, lower norm for the generalising algorithm at matched logits, and slower learning of that algorithm. The authors then hypothesise that memorisation becomes less efficient as the number of independent examples grows while a reusable rule does not, creating a critical dataset size. The paper demonstrates the predicted broad-to-narrow loss of test accuracy and reports partial test-accuracy plateaus near a seed-dependent crossover. Competing solutions, slow hidden progress, norm bias, and data-size transitions all predate this paper, so the defensible novelty is the particular logit-per-norm operationalisation and the semi-/ungrokking predictions rather than the two-circuit premise itself.

anchors.section: Related-work comparison with Davies et al.

key_findings.claim: The minimal example is a transparent existence illustration, not evidence that learned neural circuits have the proposed properties or that those properties are sufficient in realistic networks.
key_findings.evidence: The example hard-codes perfect train-and-test and train-only lookup tables, assigns the generalising table a smaller reference norm, and manually makes its second scalar subweight much smaller so it learns later. Its negative controls reverse the imposed efficiency or equalise the imposed speed and remove the grokking-shaped curve. This usefully checks the internal narrative, but the desired algorithms, relative norm, and time-scale separation are built into the construction; the paper itself cautions that it is not a quantitative model of existing grokking systems. Calling the ingredients sufficient is therefore an existence claim for this designed scalar simulation, not a sufficient-condition theorem for learned networks.

anchors.section: Appendix C simulation equations and hyperparameters

key_findings.claim: The asserted monotone efficiency curves and a unique critical dataset size are heuristics, not consequences of the stated objective or the theorem.
key_findings.evidence: The argument says an added example should force a memoriser to spend more norm while leaving a rule circuit unchanged. Yet cross-entropy is averaged over the dataset, an added easy or redundant example can lower the average loss at unchanged parameters, the learned circuit family can change with data, and optimisation can reach different minima. No theorem establishes monotonicity, existence, uniqueness, or seed-independent calibration of the crossover. The experiments estimate the threshold from the same task family and later report strong seed and initialisation dependence rather than an independently predicted held-out threshold.

anchors.section: Seed variance and semi-grokking search range

key_findings.claim: Figure 3 provides a useful qualitative scaling signature, but its C_mem and C_gen datasets do not isolate the two competing mechanisms inside the same trained model.
key_findings.evidence: The memory-only proxy trains on random labels and assigns the entire network norm to memorisation. The generalisation-only proxy uses structured labels, large datasets, and retains runs only when more than 95% of logit norm lies in a predefined trigonometric subspace. Runs vary seed, weight decay, and dataset size, and the conclusion comes from geometric logit buckets and visual isologit curves despite substantial seed spread. Thus the panels compare differently constructed tasks and post-selected networks rather than matched interventions on coexisting circuits, and they provide no regression, uncertainty interval, or out-of-sample crossover prediction.

anchors.section: Appendix A model and optimiser details

key_findings.claim: Raw Euclidean parameter norm is not an intrinsic, function-level measure of circuit efficiency, so the central empirical statistic is vulnerable to reparameterisation and shared-parameter confounds.
key_findings.evidence: The theory defines each circuit as a fixed object with a reference norm and assumes a separable power-law norm after scalar rescaling. In an actual multilayer network, inverse rescaling of adjacent homogeneous layers can preserve logits while changing layer norms, and attention, LayerNorm, biases, parameter sharing, overlap, and cancellation further break the additive fixed-circuit picture. The illustrative homogeneity motivation uses a bias-free ReLU network, while the simulation sets a non-integer effective depth of 1.2 and the Transformer is not literally that homogeneous model. A parameter-space norm can still be a useful optimiser-dependent signal, but it is not a circuit-invariant efficiency measure.

anchors.section: Appendix D.1 fixed separable circuit model

key_findings.claim: Ungrokking is a real and useful stress test in these synthetic tasks, but it does not causally identify circuit-efficiency reallocation.
key_findings.evidence: Models first train on the full finite task to perfect accuracy and then continue on a reduced subset, after which held-out points from the original full task can lose accuracy while retained training accuracy remains perfect. Modular addition shows a sharp transition over seven subset sizes and ten seeds, and nine additional modular or group tasks often show analogous declines after 100,000 reduced-data steps. However all evaluation points were already seen in the full-data phase, so the experiment measures retention or catastrophic forgetting under subsetting rather than fresh out-of-distribution generalisation. There is no circuit ablation, patching, norm-constrained control, or comparison with ordinary overfitting mechanisms that uniquely attributes the behavior to the proposed two circuits.

key_findings.claim: The claimed dataset-size threshold is strongly path-dependent, and the broad claim that it is independent of weight decay is supported only approximately and at finite horizons.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix reports an apparent modular-addition threshold around 2,000 from scratch but roughly 800 to 1,000 after full-data generalising pretraining, and later notes that the pretrained run reaches a different lower-loss minimum. Figure 4's coloured weight-decay curves nearly overlap for one modular task, but Figure 8 contains visible task-specific separation and stops every reduced-data run at 100,000 steps without a convergence diagnostic. These observations support a robust qualitative subset-size transition in some settings, not a universal state function D_crit or weight-decay independence at convergence.

anchors.section: Appendix A scratch versus pretrained thresholds

key_findings.claim: The semi-grokking experiments establish long-lived and sometimes repeated partial-accuracy plateaus, but not a stable mixed-circuit equilibrium at convergence.
key_findings.evidence: The sweep contains 200 runs: ten seeds for each of twenty dataset sizes between 1,500 and 2,050. At least six runs end at partial accuracy at the chosen horizon, while many others pass through partial plateaus before fully generalising. The detailed dataset-size-1,532 trajectory is explicitly cherry-picked, remains near 0.55 test accuracy for roughly ten million epochs, and then reaches full accuracy; the authors say many apparently semi-grokked runs might fully grok if trained longer and that their theory does not strictly determine whether a mixed equilibrium occurs. No direct circuit measurement establishes equal efficiencies in the partial runs, so the evidence is horizon-censored plateau behavior rather than convergence to the claimed balance.

anchors.section: Section 4.3 theory does not select the semi-grokking case

key_findings.claim: The trigonometric-versus-memory decomposition in Figures 9 and 10 is an assumption-laden logit projection, not a direct measurement of a memorisation circuit or norm reallocation.
key_findings.evidence: The method projects the complete modular-addition logit tensor onto a known Fourier subspace and labels every residual logit component as C_mem because the actual memorisation algorithm is unknown and the analysis assumes only two important circuit families. The appendix explicitly warns that correlated logits leak across the projection, can overestimate C_gen and underestimate C_mem, and can yield large negative memory correct logits; it also acknowledges that a raw correct-class logit is not meaningful without competing logits. Figure 9 is one randomly selected run, and Figure 10 uses models initialised from a full-data generalising solution. These diagnostics are hypothesis-generating proxies, not independent evidence that a named circuit weakens causally.

anchors.section: Appendix B residual definition and admitted flaws

key_findings.claim: There is a material optimiser/objective mismatch between the mechanism proved and the experiments run.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 2 treats weight decay as an explicit alpha times one-half squared-norm loss, and the local-minimum intuition and Theorem D.4 analyse that scalar objective. The Transformer experiments instead use full-batch AdamW, whose decay is decoupled from the adaptively preconditioned loss gradient and whose fixed points do not generally minimise the stated L2-regularised objective. Decoupled decay can still create a norm bias, but the theorem cannot be transferred to the reported experimental stationary points without an AdamW-dynamics derivation or matched explicit-L2 SGD controls.

anchors.section: Appendix D.1 optimiser and objective assumptions

key_findings.claim: Theorem D.4 is a narrow global-allocation result for identical fixed circuits, not a theorem about learning, and its case-two proof invokes a false lemma.
key_findings.evidence: The theorem assumes every circuit produces exactly the same full vector of logits on every training input, nonnegative scalar weights, fixed positive reference norms, a separable power-law total norm, and a global minimiser. Under those assumptions its allocation formula is repairable and case one is sound, but it establishes neither gradient-descent reachability, circuit discovery, local-minimum structure, nor shared neural parameters. Lemma D.3 claims that for all sufficiently small epsilon, x^r-(x-epsilon)^r exceeds a fixed positive delta times r x^(r-1)-c. As epsilon tends to zero the left side tends to zero while that right side stays positive; x=1, r=2, c=1 is a concrete counterexample. The proof divides by delta where a difference quotient requires epsilon, and case two uses the lemma on page 27. Replacing the fixed delta multiplier by epsilon and adding x>0, c>0, alpha>0, P_i>0, and 0<epsilon<delta assumptions repairs the local step and plausibly the theorem, but the published proof is invalid as written.

Case two invocation of Lemma D.3

key_findings.claim: Appendix C's printed simulation objective cannot reproduce the stated alpha setting because the weight-decay coefficient is absent from the displayed train and test losses.
key_findings.evidence: The main text defines L as cross-entropy plus alpha times one-half squared norm. Table 1 lists alpha=0.005, but the Appendix C train and test formulas simply add L_wd and then define L_wd as P_g-prime squared plus P_m-prime squared, omitting both alpha and the one-half factor. The printed test loss also includes regularisation, unlike the usual held-out cross-entropy quantity. The exact arXiv source contains the same formulas, and no code is linked or present in the source archive, so a reviewer cannot determine whether the plotted simulation used alpha, used an implicit convention, or followed the printed equation.

anchors.section: Appendix C Table 1 and displayed losses

key_findings.claim: The proof and algorithm appendices contain two additional local mathematical errors that are repairable but reduce reproducibility confidence.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B prints the cosine addition identity with cos(omega_k a) twice where the second factor must be cos(omega_k b), while the surrounding sine identity and Figure 11 make the intended expression clear. The caption also says omega is a multiple of 2 pi even though omega_k=2 pi k/p; p times omega_k is the multiple. These are local typographical errors rather than failures of the Fourier projection idea, but they persist in the exact cached source and should be corrected alongside the more consequential false lemma and omitted alpha.

anchors.section: Continuation of the Fourier projection definition

key_findings.claim: The empirical scope is much narrower than the paper's general explanation: the strongest evidence is one small Transformer and artificial finite algorithmic tasks, with no causal circuit intervention or scale test.
key_findings.evidence: The main experiments use a one-layer decoder Transformer with model width 128, head width 32, four heads, and MLP width 512 on modular arithmetic over p=113. Ungrokking extends to additional modular and group-composition tasks, but there are no natural-data tasks, deeper or larger models, alternative agent classes, compute scaling, or functional circuit patching. The paper itself identifies weight-decay-free grokking as its largest limitation and concedes that realistic tasks may have many overlapping circuits for which efficiency is hard to define. The results therefore support a provocative mechanism in a controlled test bed, not a universal account of grokking.

anchors.section: Appendix A architecture and training setup

key_findings.claim: As of the audit date, later primary work makes circuit efficiency one useful hypothesis among several competing and sometimes causally stronger explanations, not a settled mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: Subsequent studies exhibit grokking without weight decay, under non-Euclidean regularisers, in linear and kernel-like models, near separability and numerical-stability transitions, and under causal interventions on structure, logit scale, weight direction, and circuit synchronisation. Several results show that Euclidean norm can rise while generalisation improves or that direction and representation control circuit identity while magnitude mainly affects delay. These findings do not erase the target's semi-/ungrokking contribution, but they undercut a universal inference from correlated norm and logits to a two-circuit causal mechanism.

method.core_idea: Model grokking as competition between a rapidly learned memorising circuit and a slowly learned but more logit-efficient generalising circuit. Weight decay is proposed to reallocate parameter norm toward the circuit that achieves the same training logits with less norm, while dataset size changes the relative efficiency of memorisation and generalisation.
method.mechanism: A fast C_mem circuit first fits the finite training set and yields poor held-out performance. A slower C_gen circuit gradually appears. If C_gen produces larger task-relevant logits for a fixed parameter norm, the explicit norm penalty should favour increasing C_gen and decreasing C_mem even after train accuracy saturates, producing delayed generalisation. Because a reusable rule is hypothesised to retain its efficiency as dataset size D grows while item-wise memorisation becomes more costly, their efficiency curves should cross at D_crit. Training well above the crossover should grok, continuing a grokked model on a much smaller subset should ungrok, and training near the crossover may retain a mixture and partially generalise. The paper tests this with a designed lookup-table simulation, random-label and Fourier-selected efficiency proxies, dataset-shrink experiments, long semi-grokking sweeps, and a fixed-circuit global-allocation theorem.
assumptions: Training performance is dominated by two meaningful circuit families, one generalising and one memorising.
Both circuit families can fit the same training examples and their effects combine approximately additively in logit space.
Circuit strength can be represented by nonnegative scalar multipliers on otherwise fixed circuits.
Raw Euclidean parameter norm decomposes additively or by a separable power law across circuits.
Logits per unit parameter norm is an intrinsic and comparable notion of circuit efficiency.
The generalising circuit is learned more slowly than the memorising circuit.
Weight decay is the dominant late-phase selection pressure that moves norm from C_mem to C_gen.
The explicit L2-regularised objective used in the theory is representative of decoupled AdamW dynamics.
A reusable generalising algorithm retains approximately constant efficiency as more examples are added.
A memorising algorithm becomes monotonically less efficient with dataset size.
The two efficiency curves have a meaningful, sufficiently stable crossover D_crit.
Random-label training isolates memorisation without materially changing the relevant optimisation geometry.
More than 95% Fourier-subspace logit norm identifies a generalising-only solution without harmful selection bias.
All logits outside the known trigonometric subspace can be treated as memorisation.
Correct-class logit and whole-model norm are adequate surrogates for matched cross-entropy and circuit-specific norm.
Previously seen examples omitted from the reduced subset are a suitable test set for ungrokking.
Fixed training horizons are long enough to stand in for convergence in semi-grokking and multi-task ungrokking.
Behavior in one-layer Transformers on finite arithmetic tasks transfers to broader neural-network grokking.

techniques.role: Represents training as competition between a memorising and a generalising algorithm implemented by circuit families.
Defines circuit efficiency through the parameter norm required to produce a given logit scale.
Hard-codes train-only and train-and-test lookup tables and learns scalar subweights to create a minimal grokking curve.
Uses products of two subweights and asymmetric initialisation to impose different learning speeds.
Reverses relative efficiency or equalises learning speeds to show the designed simulation loses its grokking transition.
Uses random labels to construct a putative memorisation-only model for the efficiency sweep.
Selects putative generalisation-only runs whose logits lie more than 95% in a modular-addition Fourier subspace.
Geometrically buckets correct-class logits and visualises model norm versus dataset size at approximately fixed logit.
Continues a fully grokked model on a reduced subset to test for loss of held-out accuracy.
Runs 200 long trainings around an estimated critical data range to search for partial-accuracy plateaus.
Projects the full modular-addition logit tensor onto known trigonometric directions as a C_gen proxy.
Labels all nontrigonometric residual logits as C_mem because the memorisation algorithm is not identified.
Derives a global-minimiser allocation across fixed identical-logit circuits under a separable norm model.
Uses accuracy, loss, norm, logit, and dataset-size plots to diagnose grokking, ungrokking, and partial plateaus.

evaluations.metric: Train loss, test loss, total parameter norm, and learned scalar circuit strengths over optimisation steps
evaluations.result: The imposed fast but inefficient memoriser fits first; the imposed slow but efficient generaliser later replaces it and produces a grokking-shaped test transition with falling norm.
evaluations.baseline: Reversing relative efficiency or equalising imposed learning speeds removes grokking, but the algorithms, efficiency ordering, and speed ordering are hard-coded rather than learned.

evaluations.setting: Random-label modular-addition models as C_mem-only proxies
evaluations.metric: Whole-model norm versus dataset size in six geometric correct-logit buckets
evaluations.result: At approximately fixed correct logit, visual isologit curves tend upward with dataset size, consistent with increasing memorisation cost.
evaluations.baseline: No structured-label matched control, circuit-specific norm, fitted slope, uncertainty interval, or held-out threshold prediction is reported.

evaluations.setting: Large structured modular-addition runs selected as C_gen-only proxies
evaluations.metric: Whole-model norm versus dataset size at fixed correct-logit buckets
evaluations.result: The visual curves are approximately flat across dataset sizes, consistent with a reusable trigonometric algorithm.
evaluations.baseline: Runs are selected for more than 95% trigonometric logit norm and compared with a different random-label task; seed variance is substantial.

evaluations.metric: Final test accuracy versus reduced dataset size across weight-decay values
evaluations.result: Accuracy changes sigmoidally from near zero to one as the retained subset grows, with coloured weight-decay curves nearly overlapping in the main task.
evaluations.baseline: The omitted examples were previously trained, no ordinary-forgetting or matched-reinitialisation baseline is shown, and circuit reallocation is not intervened on.

evaluations.metric: Test accuracy over epochs for seven geometric reduced-data sizes and ten seeds
evaluations.result: Small subsets commonly lose nearly all test accuracy, large subsets retain accuracy, and some intermediate trajectories end at partial accuracy.
evaluations.baseline: All runs start from a full-data solution; the threshold differs markedly from scratch training and train accuracy is stated rather than plotted.

evaluations.setting: Nine additional modular arithmetic and symmetric-group tasks
evaluations.metric: Test accuracy after 100,000 reduced-subset steps versus dataset size and weight decay
evaluations.result: Many tasks show clear loss of held-out accuracy after subsetting, sometimes to nearly zero.
evaluations.baseline: A fixed 100,000-step endpoint has no convergence diagnostic, task-specific weight-decay separation remains, and no natural task or larger architecture is included.

evaluations.setting: Two hundred modular-addition trainings near estimated D_crit
evaluations.metric: Test-accuracy trajectories for ten seeds at twenty dataset sizes from 1,500 to 2,050
evaluations.result: At least six runs end at partial accuracy at the chosen horizon, while many others exhibit long transient partial plateaus or multiple phase changes.
evaluations.baseline: No censoring-aware convergence analysis, stability test, independent D_crit calibration, or direct circuit-balance measurement is supplied.

evaluations.metric: Train/test accuracy, train/test loss, and norm over roughly thirty-two million epochs
evaluations.result: The explicitly cherry-picked run stays near 0.55 test accuracy for roughly ten million epochs before reaching full accuracy and later shows an unexplained test-loss rise.
evaluations.baseline: The trajectory demonstrates a long transient rather than convergence; the interpretation in terms of multiple increasingly efficient circuits is speculative.

evaluations.setting: Fourier-projected analysis of one randomly selected grokking run
evaluations.metric: Projected C_gen correct logit, residual C_mem correct logit, loss, and whole-model norm
evaluations.result: The trigonometric proxy rises as norm falls and eventually dominates the residual proxy near test improvement.
evaluations.baseline: The projection is acknowledged to leak, correct logits are gauge-dependent, every residual is called memory, and no ablation establishes causal necessity.

evaluations.metric: Trigonometric-to-residual logit ratio and test accuracy versus dataset size at bucketed total norm
evaluations.result: Larger datasets allocate more projected logit toward the trigonometric subspace and attain higher accuracy.
evaluations.baseline: Runs begin from a full-data C_gen solution, reach a different lower-loss minimum than scratch runs, and therefore do not test path-independent global convergence.

evaluations.metric: Analytic global-minimiser support and relative scalar weights as functions of circuit norm, effective depth, and norm exponent
evaluations.result: The intended result selects only minimum-norm circuits when effective depth is at least the norm exponent, and otherwise assigns every circuit positive weight with a power-law preference for smaller reference norm.
evaluations.baseline: The result assumes identical train-logit vectors and fixed separable circuits; case two uses a false lemma but is locally repairable and says nothing about network learning dynamics.

limitations: Circuit efficiency is defined with raw Euclidean parameter norm, which is not invariant to function-preserving reparameterisation and is hard to allocate across shared parameters.
The theory assumes fixed, separable, additive circuit families even though real Transformer mechanisms overlap, interact, and change during training.
The strongest experiment uses only a one-layer width-128 Transformer and finite synthetic arithmetic or group tasks.
No causal ablation, activation patch, circuit injection, norm clamp, or counterfactual edit establishes that C_gen/C_mem competition causes the observed transitions.
C_mem-only models use random labels, whereas C_gen-only models use structured labels and are post-selected by a Fourier criterion.
Correct-class logits are not invariant to additive logit shifts and do not determine cross-entropy without margins to competing classes.
Every nontrigonometric residual is labelled memorisation even though the memorisation algorithm is unknown and other circuits may contribute.
Dataset-size monotonicity and a unique D_crit are assumed rather than proved and are strongly seed- and initialisation-dependent.
Ungrokking tests forgetting of examples seen during full-data pretraining rather than generalisation to genuinely unseen cases.
Semi-grokking is horizon-censored, with an explicitly cherry-picked detailed run and no stable-equilibrium diagnostic.
The broad multi-task ungrokking panel stops at 100,000 steps without demonstrating convergence.
Experiments use AdamW while the theorem analyses an explicit L2-regularised scalar objective.
The explanation relies on weight decay even though the paper acknowledges grokking without weight decay.
Theorem D.4 concerns restrictive global optima and has an invalid published case-two proof through false Lemma D.3.
Appendix C omits alpha from the printed simulation loss despite listing alpha=0.005, and no executable artifact resolves the discrepancy.
No code, exact data splits, seed list, checkpoints, environment, hardware, or complete convergence rule was located in the paper or exact source archive.
failure_modes: A function-preserving layer rescaling changes parameter norm and reverses an apparent circuit-efficiency comparison without changing behavior.
Multiple shared or cancelling circuits make residual logit projection misattribute non-Fourier behavior to memorisation.
Random-label training changes feature-learning and optimisation geometry, so its norm curve need not estimate the memoriser used on structured data.
Post-selecting high-Fourier runs makes the generaliser look artificially stable or efficient across dataset size.
A partial-accuracy run classified as semi-grokked later fully groks, converting a claimed equilibrium into a censored transient.
Broad-to-narrow continued training produces ordinary catastrophic forgetting or overfitting even when no distinct memorising circuit competes.
Different initialisations or pretraining paths move the apparent threshold enough that one D_crit estimate fails to predict new runs.
A fixed endpoint makes weight-decay curves appear coincident even though their asymptotic behavior or rates differ.
AdamW's adaptive preconditioner and decoupled shrinkage settle at states not described by the explicit-L2 global-minimum theorem.
Raw correct-class logits rise because of a common logit offset while classification margins and cross-entropy do not improve.
A network generalises with higher L2 norm, a different regulariser, no weight decay, or a non-neural feature learner, contradicting a norm-only account.
The lookup-table simulation appears to validate the mechanism because the desired efficiency and learning-speed ordering were inserted by construction.
An implementation following Appendix C literally ignores the reported alpha value and produces dynamics inconsistent with the plotted curves.
An implementation or proof checker following Lemma D.3 encounters a false inequality as epsilon approaches zero.
reusable_insights: For evolutionary search over RL environments, deliberately create a fast instance-specific policy and a slower reusable rule policy, then vary the number of independent training situations to test whether generalisation strength improves rather than merely assuming it.

Use broad-to-narrow continued training as an environment stress test: pretrain an agent on a broad environment distribution, continue on a narrow subset, and measure retention, overspecialisation, reward hacking, and recovery separately.
Treat a long partial-performance plateau as censored data rather than convergence; use longer horizons, survival curves, checkpoint restarts, and explicit stationarity criteria.
Predict any critical environment-diversity threshold on held-out seeds, agent families, sizes, and compute budgets instead of fitting and testing it on the same sweep.

Environment validation should combine held-out transfer, exploit resistance, learning speed, sample efficiency, compute efficiency, and cross-agent rank stability rather than rely on one small agent's final return.

A small model's success is evidence of local learnability, not scaling; test whether environment rankings and learning-signal slopes remain stable across agent capacity, optimiser, horizon, and regularisation.

Prefer function-level or intervention-based measures of strategy efficiency, such as margins, minimum description length, causal ablation cost, policy compression, and transfer under counterfactual edits, over raw network parameter norm.
Separate strategy discovery from strategy attribution: identify a candidate reusable policy, then ablate, patch, or counterfactually disable it while preserving unrelated behavior.
Evolve environment generators against a modular validator stack: rule checker, exploit detector, reference solver, learning-curve evaluator, transfer evaluator, and optional semantic human review.

Human-in-the-loop labels can name strategies and flag semantic nonsense, but automated causal checks and cross-agent replication should determine whether an environment supplies reliable learning signal.
Compare explicit regularisation, decoupled optimiser decay, and implicit bias separately; similar hyperparameter names need not imply the same selection dynamics.

Reward an environment generator for positive held-out learning slopes and stable agent ordering while penalising seed variance, exploitability, horizon sensitivity, and dependence on one architecture.

Include negative controls that deliberately reverse task structure, equalise strategy learning speeds, preserve superficial statistics, or remove the reusable rule to test whether the proposed signal is specific.
When environment diversity D changes, distinguish genuinely new causal situations from duplicate or easy cases; average loss alone does not imply monotone information or memorisation cost.
open_questions: Can circuit efficiency be defined in a function-invariant way that survives layer rescaling, shared parameters, LayerNorm, attention, and overlapping computations?
Can an independently measured C_gen/C_mem crossover predict ungrokking and semi-grokking on held-out seeds without using final accuracy to tune D_crit?
Do causal ablations of the Fourier circuit and independently identified memorising subnetworks move the apparent data-size threshold as predicted?
Does semi-grokking ever converge to a stable mixed solution under a defensible stationarity criterion, or are all observed plateaus transient?
How much of ungrokking is explained by ordinary catastrophic forgetting, distribution narrowing, or optimiser path dependence rather than efficiency reallocation?
Would explicit-L2 SGD, coupled L2 Adam, and decoupled AdamW produce the same circuit allocation after matching effective shrinkage and compute?
What environment or task statistic makes memorisation cost increase with D, and when do redundancy, curriculum, or compositional reuse violate monotonicity?
Do dataset-size transitions persist on natural data, deeper networks, language models, and non-neural learners after controlling for numerical stability and feature-learning time?
Which metric best forecasts that an RL environment supplies scalable learning signal without fully training the largest target agent?
Can environment quality be certified through cross-agent scaling curves, transfer matrices, reward-hacking probes, and counterfactual policy interventions with limited human review?
When evolutionary search discovers an environment that improves a small agent, what tests distinguish a genuinely scalable curriculum from an architecture-specific exploit?
Can a learned environment generator optimise diversity and difficulty while preserving semantic validity and preventing evaluator overfitting?
How should one aggregate feasibility, novelty, causal identifiability, compute cost, and human-review burden when ranking RL-environment research ideas?

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational discovery of grokking on small algorithmic tasks, including dataset-size and weight-decay effects.
competitive_landscape.difference: The target adds a logit-per-norm circuit-selection hypothesis and the semi-grokking and dataset-shrink ungrokking predictions.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Understanding Grokking: An Effective Theory of Representation Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct representation-learning account with a memorisation-versus-structured-representation phase diagram.
competitive_landscape.difference: It explains a Goldilocks region for representation formation, whereas the target foregrounds relative logit efficiency and a critical data-size crossover.

competitive_landscape.title: The Slingshot Mechanism: An Empirical Study of Adaptive Optimizers and the Grokking Phenomenon
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct optimiser-instability explanation, especially relevant to grokking without weight decay.
competitive_landscape.difference: The target argues smooth norm-driven circuit replacement can occur without visible slingshots but concedes its own account is incomplete at zero weight decay.

competitive_landscape.title: Hidden Progress in Deep Learning: SGD Learns Parities Near the Computational Limit
competitive_landscape.relationship: Shows gradual Fourier-aligned feature amplification can stay hidden before an abrupt performance transition.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supplies an explicit slow-feature mechanism without requiring equilibrium logit-per-norm competition between two circuit families.

competitive_landscape.title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
competitive_landscape.relationship: Norm-and-loss-landscape account demonstrated beyond algorithmic data on image, language, and molecule tasks.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is much broader empirically, while the target adds relative circuit efficiency and the semi-/ungrokking predictions.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking phase transitions in learning local rules with gradient descent
competitive_landscape.relationship: Solvable local-rule and boundary-crossing models with explicit phase-transition dynamics.
competitive_landscape.difference: It gives sharper analytic dynamics but does not posit learned memorising and generalising circuits or the target's norm-efficiency crossover.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking modular arithmetic
competitive_landscape.relationship: Demonstrates modular-arithmetic grokking with vanilla gradient descent and explicit task feature maps.
competitive_landscape.difference: It identifies learned representations and includes no-weight-decay behavior, limiting the necessity of the target's decay-mediated story.

competitive_landscape.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Reverse-engineers and ablates the modular-addition Fourier circuit while separating formation from cleanup.
competitive_landscape.difference: The target uses its Fourier result but proposes a norm-based selection pressure; its own C_mem decomposition is less causal.

competitive_landscape.title: Unifying Grokking and Double Descent
competitive_landscape.relationship: The closest conceptual precursor: a fast memoriser, slow generaliser, and late inductive preference.
competitive_landscape.difference: The target's main distinction is operationalising preference as logit per norm and deriving D_crit, semi-grokking, and ungrokking.

competitive_landscape.title: A Tale of Two Circuits: Grokking as Competition of Sparse and Dense Subnetworks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-target two-circuit competition account using sparse and dense subnetworks and neuron-norm dynamics.
competitive_landscape.difference: It substantially precedes the conceptual vocabulary; the target adds an explicit efficiency definition and data-size predictions.

competitive_landscape.title: Predicting Grokking Long Before it Happens: A look into the loss landscape of models which grok
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses early spectral and learning-curve signals to forecast eventual grokking.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is diagnostic rather than an equilibrium circuit-selection theory, but demonstrates that optimiser dynamics contain predictive signal beyond static efficiency.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Dynamics
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct lazy-kernel to feature-learning theory with an explicit zero-weight-decay regime.
competitive_landscape.difference: It covers the no-decay case the target explicitly cannot explain and focuses on representation dynamics rather than circuit norm allocation.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking as a First Order Phase Transition in Two Layer Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Adaptive-kernel and statistical-physics account of abrupt feature transitions.
competitive_landscape.difference: It analytically models trainable feature dynamics without hard-coded memorising and generalising lookup circuits.

competitive_landscape.title: Dichotomy of Early and Late Phase Implicit Biases Can Provably Induce Grokking
competitive_landscape.relationship: Proves a long early kernel-like phase followed by a late min-norm or max-margin phase.
competitive_landscape.difference: It gives a rigorous optimisation transition in neural settings rather than assuming slow and fast scalar circuit strengths.

competitive_landscape.title: To grok or not to grok: Disentangling generalization and memorization on corrupted algorithmic datasets
competitive_landscape.relationship: Identifies and prunes memorising neurons while retaining generalising representations under label corruption.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supports coexistence of solution types but provides more component-level causal evidence and compares several regularisers.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Networks Always Grok and Here is Why
competitive_landscape.relationship: Explains delayed generalisation and robustness through migration of local spline-region complexity on realistic vision data.
competitive_landscape.difference: It has broader task and architecture scope and does not require a two-circuit logit-efficiency decomposition.

competitive_landscape.title: Why Do You Grok? A Theoretical Analysis on Grokking Modular Addition
competitive_landscape.relationship: Formal analysis of early kernel failure and later bounded-norm feature learning for modular addition.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies how the generalising representation is found, which the target's fixed lookup-table model assumes away.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking Group Multiplication with Cosets
competitive_landscape.relationship: Mechanistically reverse-engineers group-multiplication circuits with subgroup and coset structure.
competitive_landscape.difference: It shows that actual learned algorithms can be task-specific and supports causal circuit analysis rather than a generic residual label.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokfast: Accelerated Grokking by Amplifying Slow Gradients
competitive_landscape.relationship: Causally accelerates grokking by amplifying slow gradient components across multiple domains.
competitive_landscape.difference: It intervenes on the proposed slow-learning signal directly and does not require measuring logit-per-norm circuit efficiency.

competitive_landscape.title: Progress Measures for Grokking on Real-world Tasks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Evaluates activation sparsity, weight entropy, and local circuit-complexity proxies on real-world tasks.
competitive_landscape.difference: It broadens progress measurement beyond L2 norm and challenges treating Euclidean norm as the primary causal statistic.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking at the Edge of Numerical Stability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Attributes delay to cross-entropy logit scaling and Softmax Collapse and uses StableMax and gradient interventions.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supplies strong causal alternatives and enables or accelerates grokking without the target's weight-decay-mediated circuit competition.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking Beyond the Euclidean Norm of Model Parameters
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct generalisation of norm-based grokking to sparsity, low rank, and other explicit or implicit regularisers.
competitive_landscape.difference: It shows L2 norm can increase while grokking occurs, directly limiting the target's Euclidean efficiency metric.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking at the Edge of Linear Separability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Produces arbitrarily delayed generalisation in a minimal logistic setting near a separability critical point.
competitive_landscape.difference: It sharply defines memorising and generalising solutions without discrete neural circuits or a dataset-dependent norm-efficiency crossover.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergence in non-neural models: grokking modular arithmetic via average gradient outer product
competitive_landscape.relationship: Demonstrates modular-arithmetic grokking in recursive feature machines and kernel-like non-neural models.
competitive_landscape.difference: It shows task-feature emergence can suffice without neural circuit competition or ordinary network gradient descent.

competitive_landscape.title: Model Capacity Determines Grokking through Competing Memorisation and Generalisation Speeds
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current direct competition model based on measurable capacity-dependent memorisation and generalisation times.
competitive_landscape.difference: It keeps the competition picture but makes relative learning speed and capacity, rather than equilibrium parameter efficiency, primary.

competitive_landscape.title: What Does the Weight Norm Control in Grokking? Logit-Scale Mediation under Cross-Entropy
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses norm clamps and output-temperature interventions to separate weight magnitude from effective logit scale.
competitive_landscape.difference: It partly supports attention to logits but argues norm is an upstream handle rather than an intrinsic circuit-efficiency cause.

competitive_landscape.title: Circuit Synchronization Precedes Generalization: A Causal Precursor to Grokking
competitive_landscape.relationship: Introduces a circuit-progress metric, permutation controls, and a weight-decay intervention preceding generalisation.
competitive_landscape.difference: It offers a more causal circuit measurement and timing law but does not use the target's logit-per-norm efficiency proxy.

competitive_landscape.title: Structure-Specific Representational Priors Causally Control the Grokking Delay
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses matched true, sibling, random, and norm-controlled structure priors to manipulate grokking delay.
competitive_landscape.difference: It causally separates task structure from norm and argues feature-formation time, not only low-norm selection, controls delay.

competitive_landscape.title: Cross-Trajectory Chimera Interventions Reveal Dissociable Roles of Weight Magnitude and Direction in Grokking
competitive_landscape.relationship: Cross-seed interventions decompose the causal roles of parameter direction and magnitude.
competitive_landscape.difference: It finds direction transfers circuit identity while magnitude mainly modulates delay, a stronger causal decomposition than whole-model norm correlations.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a specific explanation of grokking through circuit efficiency, four confirmed predictions, and especially the novel behaviors of ungrokking and semi-grokking.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It operationalises an inductive preference as logits produced per parameter norm, proposes dataset-dependent relative efficiency and D_crit, gives a designed demonstration, measures qualitative efficiency curves, and exhibits broad-to-narrow accuracy loss plus long partial plateaus in modular tasks.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Novelty is moderate and concentrated in the logit-per-norm formulation and the semi-/dataset-shrink-ungrokking experiments. The fast memoriser/slow generaliser story, circuit competition, hidden generalising progress, norm bias, and critical data effects have close precursors. Causal support for the proposed mechanism is weak because circuit identities and norms are not independently measured or intervened on, the semi-grokking claim is censored, AdamW does not optimise the analysed objective, and later primary work supplies broader and more causal alternatives.

reviewer_notes: The review is hash-bound to the 28-page arXiv v1 export listed in source_provenance. The current export was downloaded again on 2026-08-23 and was byte-identical to the cached PDF. The current arXiv record still reports only v1, submitted 2023-09-05. The exact e-print source archive had SHA-256 5c3991e7ea014c22c505bef2997fd827612d02a0ba8675ab55d8a990f9c1666a and contained TeX, bibliography/style files, and figure assets only. A separate ICLR 2024 OpenReview forum appears to exist, but automated access returned 403 during this audit, so no identity or revision equivalence is asserted; all claims remain tied to the arXiv bytes. Every extracted page and every visual was audited: all 28 pages were rendered, a full contact sheet was inspected for blank, duplicate, clipped, or unreadable pages, and high-resolution renders of the main figures, appendix figures, equations, and proof pages were checked individually. The source contained no author code URL, and exact-title, identifier, title-plus-author, and public-author GitHub searches found no author-hosted executable artifact as of 2026-08-23; no artifact was therefore run. The Appendix C alpha omission and Lemma D.3 error were confirmed against the exact TeX source, not inferred from extraction artifacts. A later public interview with author Rohin Shah states that the brief pre-convergence test-accuracy spikes discussed around the semi-grokking plots were probably a graph-production bug; this caveat applies to those spikes, not to the visibly long partial plateaus, and is not used as evidence for any stronger claim. The competitive panel was independently checked against primary arXiv, OpenReview, and PMLR records through 2026-08-23.
